title: Throughput stability heatmap and profiling scripts
content:
Purpose:
This document captures a reproducible procedure and a small collection of loadgen scripts for building a throughput stability heatmap across arrival patterns, concurrency, and sequence-length mixes. The goal is to make our throughput benchmarks less noisy, more diagnosable, and easier to compare across runtime changes (kernel updates, quantization, batching heuristics).

Scope and motivations:
- Focus: steady-state throughput behavior and stability (variance under long runs) rather than short microbenchmarks.
- We want a 2D heatmap where X is effective concurrency and Y is client arrival coefficient (poisson vs fixed vs bursty), with cell values = stable throughput (tokens/s) and overlaid p95 latency.
- Capture and surface system counters (GPU util, GPU memory, host CPU, NVLink, I/O stalls) for each cell to aid root cause analysis.

Definitions and metrics:
- Stable throughput: median tokens/s computed from the central 60% of a run after warmup (drop first and last 20% to avoid transient edges).
- Variability score: coefficient of variation (std/mean) computed on per-second tokens/s within the same central window. Flag cells with CV > 8% for follow-up.
- Latency SLO flags: measure p50/p95/p99 on token-return latency; mark cell if p95 > target (configurable).
- Occupancy-related signals: average KV cache miss ratio, batch size distribution, GPU SM active percentage, and PCIe/NVLink transfer stalls.

Experiment design and naming convention:
- Experiment id: benchYYYYMMDD-<model>-<hw>-<arrival>-<seed>-vN (e.g., bench20240303-gptx-80g-A100v4-poisson-s1234-v1).
- Always store raw trace files (one-line JSON per request) and aggregated metrics in CSV. Raw traces must include: request_id, seq_len, start_ts, end_ts, tokens_returned, batch_id, rng_seed, worker_id.

Warmup and priming policy:
- Two-stage warmup: (1) lightweight primer: 30s of short requests (16 tokens) at 10% of target concurrency to populate model weights and lazy kernels; (2) occupancy warmup: 5 minutes at target concurrency using a realistic sequence-length distribution.
- RNG hygiene: use a deterministic seed for the client-side synthetic prompt generation; the seed is recorded in the run metadata. Vary seeds to test sensitivity but keep them consistent when comparing builds.
- Cold-primed baseline: capture a cold-start baseline (single request after service restart) for reference, but do NOT use cold-start samples in the steady-state heatmap.

Arrival patterns and load mixes:
- Three canonical arrival shapes:
  - fixed-interval: constant inter-arrival, useful to stress steady batching paths.
  - poisson: exponential inter-arrival with same mean; representative of many web workloads.
  - microburst: periodic short bursts (e.g., base rate R with bursts of 10x lasting 200ms every 10s) to probe backpressure and tail amplification.
- Sequence-length mixes:
  - short-only (<=32 tokens), medium (32-256), long-heavy (256-2048) and trended mixes (80/15/5% short/med/long). Use these axes separately or as an additional heatmap dimension via separate overlays.

Load generator configuration (example parameters):
- run_duration: 1200s (20min)
- warmup_primer: {type: short, duration_s:30, qps_fraction:0.1}  <-- this is illustrative; record as JSON in metadata file.
- concurrency_target: tested range [1,2,4,8,16,32,64,128] depending on hardware
- arrival_shape: poisson | fixed | microburst
- seq_mix: short|med|long|mixed
- rng_seed: 12345
- trace_output: s3://bench-traces/benchYYYYMMDD/...

Sampling and aggregation rules:
- Collect per-request logs at 1s resolution into a streaming aggregator (tokens/s, requests/s).
- Drop first 20% and last 20% of samples for stable-window aggregation.
- Produce CSV with columns: experiment_id, concurrency, arrival, seq_mix, sec_offset, tokens_per_sec, reqs_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, gpu_util_pct, host_cpu_pct, batch_size_mean.

Heatmap generation and interpretation:
- For each arrival/concurrency pair compute: stable_tokens_per_sec, p95_latency, variability_score. Color map cells by tokens/s and annotate cells where p95 > threshold with a red outline.
- Create a companion heatmap for system signals (GPU util, avg batch size) to correlate low throughput with resource saturation or batching inefficiencies.

Profiling hooks and low-noise measurements:
- Lightweight counters: expose per-worker counters via the runtime admin endpoint (batch size histogram, KV cache hits/misses, queue length).
- High-overhead traces: enable a sampled low-rate profiler (1 in 1000 requests) that records kernel-level timelines (CUDA timeline / Triton traces). Only enable for a subset of cells because of overhead.
- Sys-level metrics: nvidia-smi sampling (1s), dmesg/driver warnings, perf counters for CPU, and network interface counters.

When a cell fails stability checks (high CV or p95 regressions):
- Re-run the cell at least 3 times with different rng_seed values and increased run_duration (1h) to confirm persistent behavior.
- If reproducible, collect high-overhead traces for 10 minutes during the problematic window and capture full NVidia profiler logs.
- Check for correlated events in infra (node migration, IO throttling, other tenant activity).

Automation scripts and tip list:
- Keep a single orchestrator that accepts an experiment matrix (list of concurrency x arrival x seq_mix) and materializes run metadata files. This helps auditability.
- Use deterministic workload generators (we use our internal benchctl, but the following is an abstract example):
  benchctl run --model gptx --hw a100v4 --matrix conc:1,2,4,8;arrival:fixed,poisson;mix:short,med --duration 1200 --warmup "primer:30s,occupancy:300s" --seed 12345 --out s3://bench-traces/2024-03-03/
- Post-process with bench-plot to produce both tokens/s heatmap and system-signal overlays.

Quick checklist before committing baseline:
- [ ] Confirm admin counters enabled and exported to Prometheus.
- [ ] Confirm RNG seed present in metadata and raw traces.
- [ ] Ensure warmup policy was executed and recorded.
- [ ] Verify storage of raw traces in S3 with run id.
- [ ] Run a 3x sanity repeat for critical cells (median within 5%).

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Should we standardize to a single arrival shape as canonical (poisson is closest to production traffic) and use others for stress testing?
- What is an acceptable CV threshold for "stable" across different models (small models tolerate higher CV)? Proposal: start with 8% and tune per-model-class.

Appendix A: example minimal CSV schema for aggregated metrics:
experiment_id,concurrency,arrival,seq_mix,sec_offset,tokens_per_sec,reqs_per_sec,p50_ms,p95_ms,gpu_util_pct,avg_batch_size,kv_miss_ratio

Appendix B: quick run playbook (for on-call or release lead)
1) Kick off bench matrix in benchctl, note experiment id.
2) Watch admin metrics for the first 10 minutes to ensure no node-level anomalies.
3) After run, run bench-plot to generate heatmaps + CSV artifacts.
4) If any cell flagged, re-run cell with longer duration and collect profiler traces.

Notes: this doc is intentionally pragmatic and focuses on methods and reproducibility. Implementation details (benchctl flags, Prom exporter names, and plotting color scales) should be captured in the benchctl repo README and the plotting microservice docs.

Author notes: try to keep heatmap runs on isolated nodes where possible; co-located noisy tenants drastically increase variance and make debugging harder.
